todoIntro: Made-up example project for the demo video. Open items from docs/TODO.md. Work an open session is already doing is in its section above. Items a session can build have a starter prompt: open it, edit if you like, copy, and paste it into a new Claude Code session in the project folder. Name the session with the title.

sessions.name: Pantry Manager
sessions.state: Needs you: which change ships first
where: Four sessions report here. Two need you, one is running, one is done.
PAN2 and PAN4 both change the recipes table. They've agreed on the columns but not the order.

questions.title: PAN2 and PAN4 both change the recipes table. Which ships first?
questions.note: PAN2's change is an index, so it's small. PAN4 adds two columns and needs a backfill.

options.label: PAN2 first, then PAN4 rebases
options.text: PAN2 ships first. Tell PAN4 to rebase on PAN2's branch once it's merged, then rerun its tests before asking for a deploy go.

options.label: PAN4 first
options.text: PAN4 ships first. Tell PAN2 to wait for PAN4's merge, rebase, and rerun its speed test before asking for a deploy go.

sessions.name: PAN4 Recipe import
sessions.state: Needs you: how to handle duplicates
where: Imports recipes from a pasted link or a photo of a recipe card.
Test import of 200 recipes: 31 were already in the pantry under a slightly different name.

questions.title: When an imported recipe matches one you already have, what should happen?
questions.note: A match means the same title and at least 80% of the same ingredients.

options.label: Merge into the one you have
options.text: Merge a matching import into the existing recipe: keep my title and notes, add any ingredients or steps the import has that mine doesn't, and list every merge on the import summary so I can undo one.

options.label: Skip it
options.text: Skip a matching import and leave my existing recipe untouched. Show the skipped ones on the import summary.

options.label: Keep both
options.text: Keep both. Save the import as a new recipe with "(imported)" after its title, and show both on the import summary.

sessions.name: PAN2 Search speed
where: Recipe search went from 2.4 s to 0.3 s on staging. All 412 tests pass.
One migration: an index on recipes.title and recipes.ingredients.

questions.title: Deploy the search speed change?
questions.note: A relayed yes approves building, not shipping. For a production deploy, type go in PAN2 yourself.

options.label: Deploy now
options.text: Go. Apply the migration and deploy now, then send Pantry Manager a done update with the commit.

options.label: Hold until tomorrow
options.text: Hold the deploy until tomorrow morning. Keep the branch pushed and ready.

sessions.name: PAN3 iPhone build
sessions.state: Running: waiting on the Mac mini
where: The iPhone app builds and passes its tests here.
The signed build has to run on the Mac mini, which has the signing certificate. The prompt for it is below.

pastes.title: Prompt for a Claude Code session on the Mac mini
pastes.to: a new Claude Code session on the Mac mini
pastes.note: Paste this as-is. It has everything that session needs.
pastes.text:
<context>
Pantry's iPhone app is on the branch pan3/iphone-build in ~/code/pantry. It builds and passes its tests on the MacBook. This Mac mini has the App Store signing certificate.
</context>

<instructions>
1. Pull the branch pan3/iphone-build.
2. Run the signed release build with the scheme PantryRelease.
3. Upload it to TestFlight as build 1.4 (12).
</instructions>

<output>
The TestFlight build number, or the first error the build hit.
</output>

starter.title: PAN5 Shared shopping lists
starter.prompt:
<context>
Pantry (~/code/pantry) makes a shopping list from the week's recipes, but only for one person. Households want one list they can all tick off. House rules are in the repo CLAUDE.md. The lists live in the shopping_lists table.
</context>

<instructions>
1. Mock the sharing flow (invite, who ticked what) and show me.
2. After my OK, build it in your own worktree. Ask before any migration.
3. Deploy only when I type go in this session.
</instructions>

<output>
The mockup first, then the shipped feature with a screenshot and the commit.
</output>

starter.title: PAN6 Nutrition labels
starter.prompt:
<context>
Pantry (~/code/pantry) stores each recipe's ingredients and amounts but shows no nutrition. Users asked for calories, protein, carbs and fat per serving. House rules are in the repo CLAUDE.md.
</context>

<instructions>
1. Propose where the numbers come from and show me one recipe's label.
2. After my OK, build it in your own worktree.
3. Deploy only when I type go in this session.
</instructions>

<output>
The proposal and sample label first, then the shipped feature with a screenshot.
</output>
